Under modern [[Indonesian orthography]], his last name would be spelled as '''Joyohadikusumo''', {{ipa|id|d͡ʒojohadikuˈsumo|lang}}.}} (born 17 October 1951) is an Indonesian politician, businessman, and retired military officer who has served as the eighth [[president of Indonesia]] since 2024. He previously served as the 26th [[List of Ministers of Defense (Indonesia)|minister of defence]] under President [[Joko Widodo]] from 2019 to 2024. Prabowo is Indonesia's third president to have a military background after [[Suharto]] and [[Susilo Bambang Yudhoyono]] and is the oldest first-term president in Indonesian history. Prabowo graduated from the [[Indonesian Military Academy]] in 1970 and primarily served in the Special Forces ([[Kopassus]]) until he was appointed to lead the Strategic Reserves Command ([[Kostrad]]) in 1998. Djojohadikusumo.jpg|thumb|left|Prabowo at 12 years old (standing right), with his siblings and grandparents, [[Margono Djojohadikusumo]] and Siti Katoemi Wirodihardjo]] Prabowo's father, [[Sumitro Djojohadikusumo]] (1917–2001), was originally from [[Gombong]], [[Kebumen Regency|Kebumen]]. He was an economist who served as former President [[Sukarno]]'s minister for the economy and [[Suharto]]'s [[Ministry of Research and Technology/National Research and Innovation Agency (Indonesia)|minister for research and technology]].Ready Susanto, ''Mari mengenal kabinet Indonesia'' [Let's know the cabinet of Indonesia], Lazuardi Buku Utama, Jakarta, 2011. Sumitro named Prabowo after his own younger brother who was killed in an incident against [[Lengkong incident|Japanese forces in Lengkong, Tangerang]] during the [[Indonesian National Revolution]].Friend (2003), p. 323 Prabowo's mother, [[Dora Marie Sigar]] (1919–2008), was a [[Protestant Christian]] of [[Minahasan people|Minahasan]] and [[German Indonesians|German]] descent, who originated from the Sigar-Maengkom family in Langowan, [[North Sulawesi]].{{Cite book|title=Christianity in Indonesia: Perspectives of Power|last=Schröter|first=Susanne|date=2010|page=311|publisher=LIT Verlag Münster|isbn=978-3-643-10798-5}} Her father was a member of the [[Volksraad (Dutch East Indies)|Volksraad of the Dutch East Indies]]. They were married in [[Matraman]], [[East Jakarta]]. Prabowo has two older sisters, Bianti Djojohadikusumo, who was born in 1946 and Maryani Djojohadikusumo, who was born in 1948.{{Cite web |title=Prabowo Subianto dan Keluarganya |url=https://kumparan.com/kumparannews/prabowo-subianto-dan-keluarganya |access-date=22 June 2023 |website=kumparan |language=id-ID |archive-date=22 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230622133525/https://kumparan.com/kumparannews/prabowo-subianto-dan-keluarganya |url-status=live }} His only brother, [[Hashim Djojohadikusumo]], was born in 1953. Prabowo's eldest sister, Bianti, is married to [[J. Soedradjad Djiwandono]], Governor of Bank Indonesia from 1993 until 1998, whilst her sister, Maryani, was married to a French expatriate entrepreneur, Didier Lemaistre who died in 2018. Prabowo's brother, Hashim, is one of the wealthiest businessmen in Indonesia with assets across the globe from Indonesia to Europe and North America. Due to his father's political exile borne from differences with Sukarno in the 1960s, they lived in self-exile, notably in countries such as Switzerland, Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, and the United Kingdom.{{cite web|url=http://www.thejakartaglobe.com/coverstory/hashims-new-horizons/495099|title=Hashim's new horizons|work=Jakarta Globe|access-date=10 May 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130318144935/http://www.thejakartaglobe.com/coverstory/hashims-new-horizons/495099|archive-date=18 March 2013|url-status=dead}} During his high school years, he studied at [[Victoria Institution]] in [[Kuala Lumpur]], Malaysia.{{cite web|url=https://www.nst.com.my/news/nation/2019/11/538880/prabowo-recalls-childhood-days-kl|title=Prabowo recalls childhood days in KL|work=New Straits Times|date=15 November 2019 |access-date=15 November 2019|archive-date=15 November 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191115054334/https://www.nst.com.my/news/nation/2019/11/538880/prabowo-recalls-childhood-days-kl|url-status=live}} Between 1966 and 1968, the family lived in London, where Prabowo attended and graduated from the [[American School in London|American School]].{{Cite web|date=2 February 2024 |title=Riwayat Pendidikan Prabowo Subianto: SD-SMA di Luar Negeri-Kuliah AKABRI|url=https://www.detik.com/edu/detikpedia/d-7173241/riwayat-pendidikan-prabowo-subianto-sd-sma-di-luar-negeri-kuliah-akabri|website=Detik|language=id-ID}}The American School in London – 1968: Gateway, p. 32 [yearbook] Sumitro subsequently encouraged his son to attend a military academy. According to peers and observers, Prabowo was strategic and had an appetite for political power. Sumitro himself came from a political background. His father, [[Margono Djojohadikusumo]], was the founder of the country's first state bank [[Bank Negara Indonesia]] (BNI), the first leader of Indonesia's provisional [[Supreme Advisory Council]] (DPA), and a member of the [[Investigating Committee for Preparatory Work for Independence]] (BPUPK) that drafted the steps for [[Proclamation of Indonesian Independence|Indonesia's independence]].Djojohadikusumo, Margono (2000). ''Kenang-Kenangan dari Tiga Zaman''. Penerbit Indira. Prabowo is the third generation of a family that has served political positions in Indonesia since its independence in 1945. Prabowo and Titiek have a son, [[Didit Hediprasetyo]], who lived in [[Boston]] before settling in Paris to pursue a career in fashion design. While his son has shown little interest in politics, Prabowo is an uncle to Gerindra politicians [[Thomas Djiwandono]], [[Budi Djiwandono]], [[Aryo Djojohadikusumo]], and [[Rahayu Saraswati|Rahayu Djojohadikusumo]], who will together continue the Djojohadikusumo political lineage.http://www.thejakartapost.com/news/2011/02/06/didit-meets-parisian-haute-couture's-challenge.html {{Dead link|date=February 2022}} ==Military career== ===Military academy and service=== {{See also|Indonesian occupation of East Timor|Papua conflict}} [[File:Danjen Kopassus Prabowo Subianto.jpg|thumb|Prabowo as Commandant General of [[Kopassus]]]] Prabowo enrolled in the [[Indonesian Military Academy]] ({{lang|id|Akademi Militer Nasional}}) in [[Magelang]] in 1970.{{Cite book |last=Conboy |first=Kenneth |title=Kopassus : inside Indonesia's special forces |date=2003 |publisher=Equinox Pub |isbn=979-95898-8-6 |oclc=51242376 }} He graduated in 1974 with others who would gain senior leadership positions, such as [[Susilo Bambang Yudhoyono]]. In 1976, Prabowo served in the [[Indonesian Army]] Special Forces Command ([[Kopassus]]) and was assigned as the commander of Group 1 {{lang|id|Komando Pasukan Sandhi Yudha}} (Kopassandha), which was one of the Indonesian Army's Nanggala commando units in [[East Timor]], the former [[Portuguese Timor|Portuguese territory]] that [[Indonesian invasion of East Timor|Indonesia had invaded the previous year]]. Prabowo, then 26 years old, was the youngest Nanggala commander. Prabowo led the mission to capture the vice president of [[Fretilin]], who was the first prime minister of East Timor, [[Nicolau dos Reis Lobato]]. Guiding Prabowo was Antonio Lobato – Nicolau's younger brother. On 31 December 1978, Prabowo's company found and fatally shot Nicolau in the stomach as he was being escorted in [[Maubisse]], fifty kilometres south of [[Dili]]. In 1981, Captain Inf. The Army's 1997 campaign was called ''Operation Eradicate''.{{Cite journal |last1=Webster |first1=David |last2=Taylor |first2=John G. |date=2001 |title=East Timor: The Price of Freedom |url=http://dx.doi.org/10.2307/2672517 |journal=Pacific Affairs |volume=74 |issue=1 |pages=138 |doi=10.2307/2672517 |jstor=2672517 |issn=0030-851X|url-access=subscription }} [[File:Letjen Prabowo Subianto.jpg|right|thumb|Prabowo as Chief of the Indonesian Armed Forces Command and Staff School (Sesko ABRI) in his uniform with multiple decorations]] In 1996, Prabowo led [[Mapenduma hostage crisis|Operation Mapenduma]] in the mountainous terrain of [[Papua (province)|Papua]]. |archive-date=27 January 2013 |url-status=live }} On 20 March 1998, Prabowo was appointed head of the 27,000-strong Army Strategic Reserve Command ([[Kostrad]]), that Suharto had commanded in web|url=https://www.cnnindonesia.com/nasional/20230719165529-617-975332/riwayat-prabowo-dijuluki-08-sejak-berpangkat-kapten-tni|title=Riwayat Prabowo Dijuluki 08 Sejak Berpangkat Kapten TNI|first=Bimo|last=Wiwoho|date=20 July 2023|website=[[CNN Indonesia]]|language=id|trans-title=Prabowo's History of Being Nicknamed 08 Since He Was a Captain|access-date=2 November 2024}} ===Role in the fall of Suharto=== {{Main|Fall of Suharto}} Less than three months after his appointment as head of Kostrad, on the first day of the [[May 1998 riots]], Prabowo urged the commander of the [[Indonesian National Armed Forces]] (ABRI), General [[Wiranto]], to let him bring his Strategic Reserve units from outside Jakarta into the city to help restore order.Friend (2005), p. 330 Hundreds of men trained by Kopassus (Prabowo's former command) were flown from [[Dili]] to [[Yogyakarta]] in chartered planes, and then on to Jakarta by train.Friend (2003), p. 331 Prabowo publicly urged Indonesians to join him to fight "traitors to the nation".Friend (2003), p. 315 On the morning of 14 May, Kopassus troops escorted young thugs from [[Lampung]] in southern Sumatra into the capital.{{Cite book |last1=Aspinall |first1=Edward |title=The last days of President Suharto |last2=Van Klinken |first2=Geert Arend |last3=Feith |first3=Herbert |date=1999 |publisher=Monash Assia Institute |isbn=0-7326-1175-X |location=Clayton |pages=57–58 |oclc=40792361 }} Thus Prabowo was accused of using his contacts in his former command to import and create trouble, while Wiranto had declined to give Prabowo's current command, Kostrad, permission to quell the existing trouble, in line with classic Javanese tactic to stir chaos to discredit a rival and/or seize power. Troops under Prabowo's command kidnapped and tortured at least nine democracy activists in the months before the [[May 1998 riots of Indonesia|May 1998 riots]].{{cite web |title=Korban yang Dikembalikan |url=http://www.kontras.org/index.php?hal=siaran_pers&id=1573 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140301053903/http://www.kontras.org/index.php?hal=siaran_pers&id=1573 |archive-date=1 March 2014 |access-date=25 February 2014 |publisher=Kontras}} In one testimony from Andi Arief, a former detainee told of being tortured for days in an unidentified location, allegedly a military camp where most of their time was spent blindfolded, while being forced to answer repeated questions, mainly concerning their political activities. The abuse included being punched, terrorised physically and mentally, and given electric shocks.{{cite web |title=Testimony of Andi Arief |url=http://www.xs4all.nl/~peace/pubeng/mov/movto/aatis.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070210175024/http://www.xs4all.nl/~peace/pubeng/mov/movto/aatis.html |archive-date=10 February 2007 |access-date=24 April 2007 |work=xs4all.nl}} Later, in 2009, two of the nine men were candidates for [[Gerindra Party|Gerindra]], Prabowo's political party, and another served as his media adviser.{{cite news |last=Thompson |first=Geoff |date=31 March 2009 |title=The Farmer Wants a Country |newspaper=ABC Foreign Correspondent |url=http://www.abc.net.au/foreign/content/2009/s2532107.htm |url-status=dead |access-date=25 kidnappings in Indonesia|kidnappings of another 13 activists]] (all of whom remain "missing") between February 1997 and May 1998.{{cite web|title=Kronik Kasus Penculikan dan Penghilangan Paksa Aktivis 1997 – 1998|url=http://www.kontras.org/data/Kronik%20kasus%20penculikan%20dan%20penghilangan%20paksa%20aktivis%201997-1998.pdf|website=kotras.org|publisher=Kontras|access-date=24 September 2014|url-status=live}} Later investigations into the May riots revealed that violence in Jakarta was the result of an internal struggle within the military elite to become Suharto's successor.{{Harvnb|Purdey|2006|p=106}} Many believed Prabowo, as Army Strategic Reserve Command (Kostrad) commander, sought to become his father-in-law's successor and coveted the commander of the Armed Forces position held by General Wiranto, who was favoured to succeed Suharto. Together with Operations Commander for Greater Jakarta ({{lang|id|Panglima Komando Operasi Jakarta Raya}}, Pangkoops Jaya) Major General [[Sjafrie Sjamsoeddin]], Prabowo aimed to terrorise opponents of the government and to show that Wiranto was "an incompetent commander who could not control disorder".{{cite news | last = Sijabat | first = Ridwan Max | title = Six years after, May 1998 tragedy still unresolved | url = http://www.thejakartapost.com/news/2004/05/13/six-years-after-may-1998-tragedy-still-unresolved.html | work = The Jakarta Post | date = 13 May 2004 | access-date = 8 June 2011 | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120310123501/http://www.thejakartapost.com/news/2004/05/13/six-years-after-may-1998-tragedy-still-unresolved.html | archive-date = 10 March 2012 | df = dmy-all }}{{Harvnb|Purdey|2006|p=107}} During August and September, the fact-finding team interviewed Prabowo, Sjafrie, and other military commanders regarding their movements during the Jakarta riots. Prabowo asserted that he was unsure of the precise movements of military forces in the capital and deferred to Sjafrie.{{Harvnb|Purdey|2006|pp=150–151}} In its final report, the fact-finding team suspected that, on the night of 14 May, Prabowo met with several Armed Forces and prominent civilian figures at the Kostrad headquarters to discuss the organisation of the violence.{{Harvnb|Purdey|2006|p=148}} However, this was later refuted by several people who attended the meeting, including prominent human rights lawyer [[Adnan Buyung Nasution]] and Joint Fact-Finding Team member, [[Bambang Widjojanto]].{{Harvnb|Purdey|2006|p=153}} Further testimonies by Prabowo{{cite web|url=http://www.etan.org/et2009/03march/22/19prabw.htm|title=Prabowo, Gerindra Fight Accusations of Past Rights Abuses|work=etan.org|access-date=24 August 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120620075940/http://www.etan.org/et2009/03march/22/19prabw.htm|archive-date=20 June 2012|url-status=live}} in the years following the investigation contradicted the team's report and led to scepticism of the team's allegations.{{Harvnb|Purdey|2006|p=154}} ===Dismissal from the military=== On 21 May 1998, Suharto announced his resignation from the presidency and Vice President [[B. J. Habibie]] took over as president. On the afternoon following Habibie's inauguration as president, Prabowo demanded of Habibie that he be put in charge of the army in place of Wiranto. However, Habibie and Wiranto actually dismissed Prabowo from his position as Kostrad commander, and the following day, announced Wiranto's appointment as minister of defence and security as well as commander of the [[Indonesian Army]], which resulted in Prabowo's dismissal. There were two versions of how this happened: the first version states that a furious Prabowo went to the Presidential Palace carrying a gun and a truck with his Kostrad troops. Because he was prevented from entering Habibie's office, he went to Suharto, who instead reprimanded him.{{Cite book |last=van Dijk |first=Cornelis Pieter |title=A Country in Despair Indonesia Between 1997 And 2000. |date=2001 |publisher=BRILL |isbn=978-90-04-43487-5 |location=Boston |pages=209–210 |oclc=1276859752 |author-link=Kees van Dijk }}{{Cite journal |last=Emmerson |first=Donald K. |date=20 May 2015 |title=Indonesia Beyond Suharto |url=http://dx.doi.org/10.4324/9781315703510 |journal=Gramedia Pustaka Utama |location=Jakarta |pages=309 |doi=10.4324/9781315703510 |isbn=978-1-317-46808-0 |access-date=23 March 2023 |archive-date=14 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240214180013/https://www.taylorfrancis.com/books/mono/10.4324/9781315703510/indonesia-beyond-suharto-donald-emmerson |url-status=live |url-access=subscription }}{{Cite book |last=Schwarz |first=Adam |title=A nation in waiting : Indonesia in the 1990s |date=1994 |publisher=Westview Press |isbn=0-8133-8881-3 |location=Boulder |pages=367–369 |oclc=30356852 }} Meanwhile, another version states that Prabowo was dismissed from his post because he was suspected of carrying out a coup against Habibie.{{Cite book |last=Habibie |first=Bacharuddin Jusuf |title=Detik-detik yang menentukan : jalan panjang Indonesia menuju demokrasi |date=2006 |publisher=THC Mandiri |isbn=979-99386-6-X |edition=1st |location=Jakarta, Indonesia |oclc=71779429 |author-link=B. J. Habibie }} It is said that after Habibie's inauguration, Wiranto reported that there was movement from Kostrad troops appearing around Habibie's residence. Habibie then ordered Prabowo to be dismissed from his post just before sunset in that day.{{cite book|last=Subroto|first=Hendro|date=2009|title=Sintong Panjaitan, perjalanan seorang prajurit para komando|location=Jakarta|publisher=Penerbit Buku Kompas|pages=11–14|isbn=978-979-709-408-9}}{{Cite web|last=Agus|first=Feri|date=2018|title=Beda Nasib Wiranto dan Prabowo Usai Soeharto Tumbang|url=https://www.cnnindonesia.com/nasional/20180516093007-20-298555/beda-nasib-wiranto-dan-prabowo-usai-soeharto-tumbang|website=[[CNN Indonesia]]|language=id-ID|access-date=1 March 2024}}{{Cite web|last=Musthafa|first=Siti Aisah Nurhalida|title='Anda Ini Presiden Naif!', Dialog Utuh Prabowo pada Habibie yang Ramai Tahun 1998|url=https://www.pikiran-rakyat.com/nasional/pr-017772096/anda-ini-presiden-naif-dialog-utuh-prabowo-pada-habibie-yang-ramai-tahun-1998?page=all|website=[[Pikiran Rakyat]]|language=id|access-date=1 March 2024}} However, Prabowo was later visited by Wiranto at his home on the weekend of 23 or 24 May and then reassigned to a non-combat role at the Armed Forces Command and General Staff College in [[Bandung]].{{cite news |last=McBeth |first=John |author-link=John McBeth |date=4 June 1998 |title=Soldiering On: Military chief faces down one threat but others loom |newspaper=Far Eastern Economic Review |url=http://www.library.ohiou.edu/indopubs/1998/05/29/0083.html |url-status=dead |access-date=25 February 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140228122813/http://www.library.ohiou.edu/indopubs/1998/05/29/0083.html |archive-date=28 February 2014}} Following an ABRI investigation in August 1998, the {{lang|id|Dewan Kehormatan Perwira}} (Officers Council of Honour) found Prabowo guilty of "misinterpreting orders" in the kidnapping of nine anti-Suharto activists in 1998.{{cite web |last=Tesoro |first=Jose Manuel |date=3 March 2000 |title=The Scapegoat? |url=http://www-cgi.cnn.com/ASIANOW/asiaweek/magazine/2000/0303/cover1.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140313050521/http://www-cgi.cnn.com/ASIANOW/asiaweek/magazine/2000/0303/cover1.html |archive-date=13 March 2014 |access-date=10 May 2012 |publisher=CNN}} Prabowo acknowledged responsibility for the kidnapping of the nine activists,Friend (2003), p. 347 and was discharged honourably from military service in November.{{cite web | title=Adu Pendapat Seputar Pilpres Ini Isi Lengkap Keppres Pemberhentian Letjen Prabowo Subianto | website=detiknews | date=20 June 2014 | url=https://news.detik.com/berita/d-2614304/ini-isi-lengkap-keppres-pemberhentian-letjen-prabowo-subianto | language=id | access-date=28 February 2024 | archive-date=23 March 2024 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240323072034/https://news.detik.com/berita/d-2614304/ini-isi-lengkap-keppres-pemberhentian-letjen-prabowo-subianto | url-status=live }} He and Wiranto denied that the discharge was a result of disciplinary action.{{Harvnb|Purdey|2006|p=155}} Later he went into voluntary exile in [[Jordan]] where he knew that country's new young King Abdullah as a fellow commander of special forces. In an interview with ''[[Asiaweek]]'' magazine in 2000, Prabowo said "I never threatened Habibie. I was not behind the riots. That is a great lie. I never betrayed Suharto. I never betrayed Habibie. I never betrayed my country. There was a certain group that wanted to make me a scapegoat, maybe to hide their involvement." Human rights groups have long questioned Prabowo's eligibility to run for president, noting that he was discharged from the Army in August 1998{{efn|Keppres No. 62/ABRI/1998 dated 20 November 1998, states that Prabowo was discharged honourably from the military, starting from the end of November.}} for "misinterpreting orders" in the abduction of the democracy activists. While that was the military's official statement, observers have long believed that it was a coup conspiracy that saw Prabowo, then the commander of the Army Strategic Reserves, given his marching orders.{{cite news|last=Sihaloho|first=Markus|title=A Checkered Past Continues to Dog Would-Be Leader|url=http://www.thejakartaglobe.com/news/checkered-past-continues-dog-leader/|access-date=30 May 2014|newspaper=Jakarta Globe|date=30 May 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140531124015/http://www.thejakartaglobe.com/news/checkered-past-continues-dog-leader/|archive-date=31 May 2014|url-status=live}} As a [[2014 Indonesian presidential election#Political parties|2014 presidential candidate]], Prabowo's past came under renewed scrutiny, with many organisations calling for him to step down. On 19 April, he was criticised by a poet made by Fahmi Habcyi which linked him to the disappearance of Widji Thukul and urged him to return Thukul as his wife is devastated hoping for her husband to return.{{Cite web |author=Sugiharto |title=Prabowo Disentil Lewat Puisi Wiji Thukul |url=https://pemilu.tempo.co/read/571757/prabowo-disentil-lewat-puisi-wiji-thukul |access-date=14 November 2023 |website=Tempo |language=en |archive-date=14 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231114143217/https://pemilu.tempo.co/read/571757/prabowo-disentil-lewat-puisi-wiji-thukul |url-status=live }} A coalition, which consisted of Imparsial, Kontras, the Setara Institute, and the Human Rights Working Group (HRWG), combined under the Civil Society Coalition Against Forgetting, visited the [[National Commission on Human Rights (Indonesia)|National Commission on Human Rights (Komnas HAM)]] in Jakarta on 7 May 2014 to urge the commission to re-investigate Prabowo.{{cite news|title=Prabowo unsuitable for president, rights campaigners say|url=http://www.thejakartapost.com/news/2014/05/07/prabowo-unsuitable-president-rights-campaigners-say.html|access-date=13 May 2014|newspaper=The Jakarta Post|date=7 May 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140514080632/http://www.thejakartapost.com/news/2014/05/07/prabowo-unsuitable-president-rights-campaigners-say.html|archive-date=14 May 2014|url-status=live}} A 27 June 2014 report indicated that an investigative journalist, [[Allan Nairn]], had been threatened with arrest "for revealing the former general's role in human rights abuses."{{Cite web|title = Journalist Allan Nairn Threatened for Exposing Indonesian Pres. Candidate's Role in Mass Killings|work = Democracy Now!|access-date = 4 July 2014|date = 27 June 2014|url = http://www.democracynow.org/2014/6/27/journalist_allan_nairn_threatened_for_exposing|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20140704000030/http://www.democracynow.org/2014/6/27/journalist_allan_nairn_threatened_for_exposing|archive-date = 4 July 2014|url-status = live}} During the 2024 presidential debate on 12 December 2023, Prabowo admitted implicitly that he had [[Budiman Sudjatmiko]] kidnapped, a violation of human rights, later Sudjatmiko had become one of his spokesperson.{{Cite web |last1=Media |first1=Kompas Cyber |date=13 December 2023 |title=Prabowo Klaim Didukung "Tapol yang Katanya Saya Culik", Budiman Sudjatmiko Langsung Berdiri Angkat Tangan |url=https://nasional.kompas.com/read/2023/12/13/17200141/prabowo-klaim-didukung-tapol-yang-katanya-saya-culik-budiman-sudjatmiko |access-date=14 February 2024 |website=KOMPAS |language=id |archive-date=26 December 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231226193116/https://nasional.kompas.com/read/2023/12/13/17200141/prabowo-klaim-didukung-tapol-yang-katanya-saya-culik-budiman-sudjatmiko |url-status=live}} Prior to the debate, Prabowo also admitted to Sudjatmiko, that he had released all activists he had kidnapped but didn't know of their later fates after released.{{Cite web |date=27 July 2023 |title=Tanyakan Isu Penculikan ke Prabowo, Budiman Sudjatmiko: Beliau Bilang Sudah Dikembalikan Semua |url=https://www.kompas.com/ |access-date=16 February 2024 |website=KOMPAS.com |language=id |archive-date=20 February 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210220205902/https://www.kompas.com/ |url-status=live }} Explaining his decision, Budiman claimed people changed after 25 years, both him and Prabowo "moved to the middle." [[Maria Catarina Sumarsih]], whose son was shot dead during the [[Semanggi shootings]] on 13 November 1998, said that Prabowo was responsible for the tragedy.{{Cite news |last1=Ratcliffe |first1=Rebecca |last2=Hariandja |first2=Richaldo |date=16 February 2024 |title='A betrayal': mother's fight for justice as Indonesia elects Suharto era figure |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/feb/16/he-must-surrender-mothers-fight-for-justice-amid-indonesian-regime-change |access-date=17 February 2024 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077 |archive-date=19 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240219025908/https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/feb/16/he-must-surrender-mothers-fight-for-justice-amid-indonesian-regime-change |url-status=live }} ==Business career== After being discharged from the military, Prabowo joined his brother [[Hashim Djojohadikusumo|Hashim Djojohadikusumo's]] business. He purchased Kiani Kertas, a paper pulp and plantation company based in Mangkajang, [[East Kalimantan]].{{cite web |last1=Nairus |first1=Vinda |last2=Klute |first2=Marianne |date=August 2005 |others=Translated by Petra Stockmann and Christoph Assheuer |title=Pulp Factory Kiani Kertas in the limelight again |url=http://www.watchindonesia.org/Kiani_eng.htm |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130810003239/http://www.watchindonesia.org/Kiani_eng.htm |archive-date=10 August 2013 |access-date=10 May 2012 |work=watchindonesia.org}} Prior to Prabowo's purchase, Kiani was owned by [[Bob Hasan]], a businessman close to former President [[Soeharto|Suharto]]. Today, Prabowo's Nusantara Group controls 27 companies in Indonesia and abroad. Prabowo's companies include Nusantara Energy ([[Energy in Indonesia|oil and natural gas]], coal), Tidar Kerinci Agung ([[Palm oil production in Indonesia|palm oil]] plantations) and Jaladri Nusantara (fishery industry).{{cite web |last1=Dhyatmika |first1=Wahyu |last2=Wahid |first2=Ismi |last3=Megarani |first3=Amandra |last4=Nilawaty |first4=Cheta |date=21 December 2010 |title=The rich who plead poverty at Directnic |url=http://www.asiaviews.org/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=775:headlinealias775 |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130809202401/http://www.asiaviews.org/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=775:headlinealias775 |archive-date=9 August 2013 |access-date=10 May 2012 |work=asiaviews.org}} Prabowo rebranded Kiani Kertas to Kertas Nusantara. The company was established in 1990 and is part of the Nusantara Energy. It controls an area of {{cvt|3,400|hectare|acre}} used for paper mills, employee housing, private schools, and various company facilities.{{cite web |last=Suprapto |first=Hadi |date=11 May 2009 |title=Bisnis Prabowo yang Menggurita |url=https://www.viva.co.id/arsip/56564-bisnis-prabowo-yang-menggurita |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141217050058/http://bisnis.news.viva.co.id/news/read/56564-bisnis_prabowo_yang_menggurita |archive-date=17 December 2014 |access-date=30 May 2014 |work=VIVA.co.id}} Kiani has been awarded ISO 900–2005 status as one of the highest quality management companies. It is reported that Kiani Kertas has been experiencing financial difficulties, and in early 2014, workers took to the streets to demand their wages which had not been paid in five months.{{cite news |last=Hidayat |first=Firman |date=20 January 2014 |editor-last=Abidien |editor-first=Zed |title=5 Bulan Tak Digaji Karyawan Prabowo Subianto Mogok |url=https://nasional.tempo.co/read/546632/5-bulan-tak-digaji-karyawan-prabowo-subianto-mogok |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140504233545/http://www.tempo.co/read/news/2014/01/20/058546632/5-Bulan-Tak-Digaji-Karyawan-Prabowo-Subianto-Mogok |archive-date=4 May 2014 |access-date=24 May 2014 |work=Tempo}} Prabowo was the wealthiest presidential candidate in the 2009 election, with assets of Rp 1.5 trillion (about US$150 million) and US$7.5 million.{{Cite web |url=http://mediacenter.kpu.go.id/berita/635-kpu-umumkan-harta-kekayaan-dan-dana-awal-kampanye-caprescawapres.html |title=KPU Umumkan Harta Kekayaan dan Dana Awal Kampanye Capres/Cawapres |access-date=10 May 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140408224634/http://mediacenter.kpu.go.id/berita/635-kpu-umumkan-harta-kekayaan-dan-dana-awal-kampanye-caprescawapres.html |archive-date=8 April 2014 |url-status=dead }} In 2007, PT Ridlatama, whose majority stakeholder was British-based Churchill PLC, conducted a geo-survey of [[East Kalimantan|eastern Kalimantan]] for [[List of countries by coal production|coal]]. Two months after the survey yielded positive results, East Kutai officials granted mining licenses to Nusantara Energy (a subsidiary of the Nusantara Group, a conglomerate owned by Prabowo's family) to operate in the area surveyed by Ridlatama. In 2010, Ridlatama's license was revoked, effectively completing Nusantara's take over of Churchill's operations. Churchill appealed to the Supreme Court of Indonesia but lost the case. In 2012, Churchill filed a case against the government of Indonesia at the [[International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes]], demanding US$2 billion in compensation. 2014 |access-date=24 May 2014 |work=tempo.co}} ==Advocacy career== ===Farmers' rights (HKTI)=== The Indonesian Farmers' Association (HKTI) was established in 1973 to advocate for the farmers' rights. Prabowo was elected President of HKTI on 5 December 2004,{{cite news |date=3 December 2004 |title=Prabowo Ikut Bursa Calon Ketua HKTI |url=http://www.tempointeraktif.com/hg/ekbis/2004/12/03/brk,20041203-74,id.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140408214429/http://www.tempointeraktif.com/hg/ekbis/2004/12/03/brk,20041203-74,id.html |archive-date=8 April 2014 |access-date=7 October 2008 |publisher=Tempointeraktif |language=id}}{{cite web |work=[[Himpunan Kerukunan Tani Indonesia]] |title=Ketua Umum Prabowo Subianto |url=http://www.hkti.or.id/dsp_home.php?fuseaction=hkti.staticfront&setLang=id&contentID=14 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080908100642/http://www.hkti.or.id/dsp_home.php?fuseaction=hkti.staticfront&setLang=id&contentID=14 |archive-date=8 September 2008 |access-date=7 October 2008 |language=id}} and he was reappointed in 2010 for a second term.{{cite web |title=Prabowo Terpilih Secara Aklamasi Pimpin HKTI |url=http://news.detik.com/read/2010/07/13/223516/1398674/10/prabowo-terpilih-secara-aklamasi-pimpin-hkti |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130810110511/http://news.detik.com/read/2010/07/13/223516/1398674/10/prabowo-terpilih-secara-aklamasi-pimpin-hkti |archive-date=10 August 2013 |access-date=10 May 2012 |work=detiknews}} ===Market traders (APPSI)=== The Indonesian Traditional Market Traders Association (APPSI) is a non-profit organisation advocating for the welfare of traders in Indonesia's traditional markets. Prabowo was elected as president of APPSI in 2008.{{cite web |date=6 August 2008 |title=Prabowo Subianto Jadi Ketua Asosiasi Pedagang Pasar |url=http://finance.detik.com/read/2008/08/06/171555/984138/4/prabowo-subianto-jadi-ketua-asosiasi-pedagang-pasar |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130810085616/http://finance.detik.com/read/2008/08/06/171555/984138/4/prabowo-subianto-jadi-ketua-asosiasi-pedagang-pasar |archive-date=10 August 2013 |access-date=10 May 2012 |work=detikfinance}} As a chairman of the organisation, Prabowo often calls for the government to limit hypermarkets by regulating their distances so as not to harm small traders. "So far, traditional market traders have always been ignored, so that when a modern market was established, the capital owners of the market traders had to be willing to be disbanded due to demolition," said Prabowo.{{Cite web |author=Pramono |date=13 August 2009 |work=Tempointeraktif |title=Tak Ada Sanksi Untuk Mega-Prabowo |url=http://www.tempointeraktif.com/hg/Pemilu2009_berita_mutakhir/2009/07/25/brk,20090725-188991,id.html |access-date=18 February 2024 |archive-date=13 August 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090813234009/http://www.tempointeraktif.com/hg/Pemilu2009_berita_mutakhir/2009/07/25/brk,20090725-188991,id.html |url-status=bot: unknown }} ===''Pencak silat'' and the IPSI=== [[File:Prabowo and Indonesian Pencak Silat Association.jpg|thumb|Prabowo opening the 2011 ''pencak silat'' [[SEA Games]] tournament held in [[Taman Mini]], [[Jakarta]]. He is the chairman of Indonesia's ''pencak silat'' organisation, the Indonesian Pencak Silat Association.]] ''[[Pencak silat]]'' is one of Indonesia's traditional martial arts. The Indonesian Pencak Silat Association (IPSI) oversees the regulation of the sport in Indonesia, develops athletes, and organises tournaments. Prabowo was elected as president of the IPSI in 2004 and was re-elected in 2012 for a third consecutive term.{{cite web |title=Lagi, Prabowo Pimpin PB IPSI |url=http://www.suaramerdeka.com/v1/index.php/read/cetak/2012/02/27/178498/Lagi-Prabowo-Pimpin-PB-IPSI |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140408233935/http://www.suaramerdeka.com/v1/index.php/read/cetak/2012/02/27/178498/Lagi-Prabowo-Pimpin-PB-IPSI |archive-date=8 April 2014 |access-date=10 May 2012 |work=suaramerdeka.com}} At the [[2011 SEA Games]] in Jakarta, ''pencak silat'' won the overall championship by winning 9 of the 18 events competed.{{Cite web |date=8 August 2008 |title=Prabowo: "Batasi Pasar Modern!" |url=http://www.inilah.com/read/detail/42647/prabowo-batasi-pasar-modern |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161011140715/http://www.inilah.com/read/detail/42647/prabowo-batasi-pasar-modern |archive-date=11 October 2016 |website=Inilah}} The IPSI's achievements under Prabowo's chairmanship were noted at the [[2018 Asian Games]], where ''pencak silat'' succeeded in contributing to 14 of the 31 gold medals won by the Indonesian contingent. Prabowo is also the president of the [[International Pencak Silat Federation]] (IPSF).{{Cite web |title=SEA Games: Indonesia raih juara umum cabang pencak silat |url=http://www.silatindonesia.com/2011/11/sea-games-indonesia-raih-juara-umum-cabang-pencak-silat/ |access-date=18 February 2024 |website=Silat Indonesia|date=16 May 2014 |archive-date=18 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240218054058/http://www.silatindonesia.com/2011/11/sea-games-indonesia-raih-juara-umum-cabang-pencak-silat/ |url-status=live }} ===Migrant workers=== The Indonesian Advocacy Service for Justice and Peace (Padma) in the [[East Nusa Tenggara]] region assessed that Prabowo played a major role in the release of Wilfrida Soik from the death penalty at the Kota Bahru Court, [[Kelantan]], Malaysia.{{Cite web |date=10 May 2014 |title=Prabowo Pelihara Anak-Anak Muda Alumni Luar Negeri |url=https://www.tempo.co/read/news/2013/10/28/078525155/Prabowo-Pelihara-Anak-anak-Muda-Alumni-Luar-Negeri |website=Tempo |access-date=18 February 2024 |archive-date=10 May 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140510185516/http://www.tempo.co/read/news/2013/10/28/078525155/Prabowo-Pelihara-Anak-anak-Muda-Alumni-Luar-Negeri |url-status=dead }} Prabowo appointed Malaysian lawyer Tan Sri Mohammad Syafei to defend Wilfrida Soik. Wilfrida is a worker from East Nusa Tenggara who was sent illegally. Wilfrida was sentenced to death for killing her employer, Yeap Seok Pen, on 7 December 2010.{{Cite web |last=Bere |first=Sigiranus Marutho |date=7 April 2014 |title=Padma NTT: Terima Kasih Prabowo Telah Selamatkan Wilfrida Soik |url=https://regional.kompas.com/read/xml/2014/04/07/1702490/Padma.NTT.Terima.Kasih.Prabowo.Telah.Selamatkan.Wilfrida.Soik |access-date=18 February 2024 |website=Kompas |language=id |archive-date=19 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240219025855/https://regional.kompas.com/read/2014/04/07/1702490/Padma.NTT.Terima.Kasih.Prabowo.Telah.Selamatkan.Wilfrida.Soik |url-status=live }} == Early political career == Using his connections to President Suharto, Prabowo and his brother worked to silence journalistic and political critics in the 1990s. Hashim unsuccessfully pressured [[Goenawan Mohamad]] to sell his outspoken and banned ''[[Tempo (Indonesia magazine)|Tempo]]'' magazine to him.Friend (2003), p. 324 As a lieutenant colonel, Prabowo invited [[Abdurrahman Wahid]] to his battalion headquarters in 1992 and warned him to stick to religion and to stay out of politics, or face unspecified actions if he continued to oppose the president.Friend (2003), pp. 203, 324 He later warned the intellectual [[Nurcholish Madjid]] (Cak Nur) to resign from the KIPP, the election monitoring unit set up by Goenawan Mohamad, which armed forces commander [[Feisal Tanjung]] had denounced as "obviously unconstitutional.""Surat Dari Redaksi" (Letter from the Editor), ''Tempo'', 6–12 Oct 98, p. 7; Schwarz, ''Nation in Waiting'', pp. 161–162, 320, 490n35. ===Golkar Party convention=== In 2004, Prabowo was one of five contenders in the {{ill|2004 Golkar Party National Convention|id|Konvensi Calon Presiden Partai Golongan Karya}} vying to become [[Golkar]] party's presidential candidate. He received the lowest number of votes, just 39, and was eliminated in the first round.{{cite book|last = Ananta|first = Aris|title = Emerging Democracy in Indonesia|url = https://books.google.com/books?id=1QpWEAtDjWMC&pg=PA67|date = November 2005|publisher = Institute of Southeast Asian Studies|location = Singapore|isbn = 978-981-230-322-6|page = 94|access-date = 24 September 2016|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20161227044854/https://books.google.com/books?id=1QpWEAtDjWMC&pg=PA67|archive-date = 27 December 2016|url-status = live}} The second round of voting was won by [[Wiranto]]. After finishing last in the party convention, Prabowo served as a member of the Golkar Advisory Council until his resignation on 12 July 2008. ===Gerindra Party=== In February 2008, Prabowo's inner circle, including [[Fadli Zon]], [[Muchdi Purwopranjono]], and Prabowo's younger brother [[Hashim Djojohadikusumo]], along with a few others established the [[Gerindra Party]]. Prabowo served as chairman of the Board of Trustees of the Central Leadership Council (DPP). He was later appointed general chairman of the party after the death of the party's previous chairman Suhardi in 2014.{{Cite web |last=Bestari |first=Fardi |date=21 November 2023 |title=Prabowo Subianto Terima Penghargaan Darjah Utama Bakti dari Presiden Singapura |url=https://foto.tempo.co/read/109909/prabowo-subianto-terima-penghargaan-darjah-utama-bakti-dari-presiden-singapura |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231122003726/https://foto.tempo.co/read/109909/prabowo-subianto-terima-penghargaan-darjah-utama-bakti-dari-presiden-singapura |archive-date=22 November 2023 |access-date=21 November 2023 |website=Tempo |language=id}} ==Vice-presidential candidacy== {{See also|2009 Indonesian presidential election}} In May 2009, Gerindra nominated Prabowo for the presidency in the [[2009 Indonesian presidential election|2009 elections]].{{cite news |last=Maslan |first=Muhammad Rizal |date=9 May 2008 |title=Datangi KPU, Partai Gerindra Usung Prabowo Sebagai Capres |language=id |publisher=Detik.com |url=https://news.detik.com/berita/d-936898/datangi-kpu-partai-gerindra-usung-prabowo-sebagai-capres |url-status=live |access-date=7 October 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080817051906/http://www.detiknews.com/index.php/detik.read/tahun/2008/bulan/05/tgl/09/time/161653/idnews/936898/idkanal/10 |archive-date=17 August 2008}} However, having won 26 out of 560 seats in the Indonesian parliament, the party did not have the required numbers, and Prabowo ran as a vice-presidential candidate to [[Megawati Sukarnoputri]], daughter of Indonesia's first president [[Sukarno]]. Prabowo and Megawati signed the Batu Tulis Agreement, which stated that:{{Cite web |last=Rafie |first=Barratut Taqiyyah |date=21 September 2014 |title=Prabowo replaces Suhardi as Gerindra chairman |url=https://english.kontan.co.id/news/prabowo-replaces-suhardi-as-gerindra-chairman |access-date=18 February 2024 |website=Kontan |language=en |archive-date=1 July 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200701043619/https://english.kontan.co.id/news/prabowo-replaces-suhardi-as-gerindra-chairman |url-status=live }} # [[Indonesian Democratic Party of Struggle|PDI-P]] and Gerindra nominated Megawati as presidential candidate and Prabowo as vice-presidential candidate in the 2009 elections. # If elected, Prabowo can control Indonesia's economic programs and policies which are "based on the principles of standing on one's own feet, being sovereign in the political field, and having a national personality in the cultural field within the framework of a presidential system" # Prabowo can determine who will be Minister of Forestry, Minister of Agriculture, Minister of Finance, Minister of State Owned Enterprises, Minister of Energy and Mineral Resources, Minister of Maritime Affairs and Fisheries, Minister of Industry, Minister of Manpower and Transmigration, Minister of Law and Human Rights, and Minister of Defence. # The government that is formed will support the PDI-P's people's program and the Gerindra's eight action programs for the prosperity of the people. # Funding for the 2009 elections will be covered 50% by Megawati and 50% by Prabowo. # Megawati shall back Prabowo as 2014 presidential election candidate. The pair, referred to colloquially by the Indonesian media as ''Mega–Pro'', earned 27% of the vote and lost to [[Susilo Bambang Yudhoyono]] and his running mate, economist [[Boediono]].{{cite news |date=28 July 2009 |title=Megawati-Prabowo team files lawsuit protesting presidential election result |newspaper=[[The Jakarta Post]] |url=http://www.thejakartapost.com/news/2009/07/28/megawatiprabowo-team-files-lawsuit-protesting-presidential-election-result.html |url-status=dead |access-date=25 February 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120923044232/http://www.thejakartapost.com/news/2009/07/28/megawatiprabowo-team-files-lawsuit-protesting-presidential-election-result.html |archive-date=23 September 2012}} The results of the KPU's manual calculation, which were announced on 25 July 2009, were not much different from the results of the [[quick count]]. Megawati and Prabowo were absent at the announcement of the official tally even though Law No. 42 of 2008 concerning Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections mandated each pair of candidates to be present in determining the official results of the presidential election.{{Cite web |last=Yudhistira |first=Angkasa |date=18 March 2014 |title=Ini Isi Perjanjian Batu Tulis Antara-Megawati dengan Prabowo |url=https://news.okezone.com/read/2014/03/18/568/956642/ini-isi-perjanjian-batu-tulis-antara-megawati-dengan-prabowo/large |access-date=18 February 2024 |website=Okezone News |language=id-ID |archive-date=18 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240218054059/https://news.okezone.com/read/2014/03/18/568/956642/ini-isi-perjanjian-batu-tulis-antara-megawati-dengan-prabowo/large |url-status=live }} ==Presidential candidacies== ===2014 general election=== {{See also|2014 Indonesian presidential election}} [[File:Prabowo Accepts Gerindra's Nomination.jpg|thumb|Prabowo accepting the [[Gerindra Party]]'s nomination rally for the 2014 presidential election in Lembah Hambalang on 17 March 2012]] In November 2011, Prabowo announced his intention to run in the [[2014 Indonesian presidential election|2014 presidential election]]. LSI Survey Says Yes |url=http://www.thejakartaglobe.com/politics/president-prabowo-lsi-survey-says-yes/500184 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120225235804/http://www.thejakartaglobe.com/politics/president-prabowo-lsi-survey-says-yes/500184 |archive-date=25 February 2012 |access-date=25 February 2012 |newspaper=[[Jakarta Globe]]}} In March 2012, Gerindra named Prabowo its 2014 presidential candidate.{{cite web |last=Faqih |first=Mansyur |date=9 May 2012 |editor-last=Muhammad |editor-first=Djibril |title=Prabowo Resmi Jadi Capres Partai Gerindra |url=http://www.republika.co.id/berita/nasional/politik/12/05/09/m3qzzg-prabowo-resmi-jadi-capres-partai-gerindra |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120512090523/http://www.republika.co.id/berita/nasional/politik/12/05/09/m3qzzg-prabowo-resmi-jadi-capres-partai-gerindra |archive-date=12 May 2012 |access-date=10 May 2012 |work=Republika Online}} The party's slogan was then changed to ''Gerindra Menang Prabowo Presiden'' (Gerindra Wins, Prabowo Becomes President).{{cite web |title=Muzani: Gerindra Menang, Prabowo Presiden |url=https://www.jpnn.com/news/muzani-gerindra-menang-prabowo-presiden |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130809140133/http://www.jpnn.com/read/2012/05/09/126854/Muzani:-Gerindra-Menang,-Prabowo-Presiden- |archive-date=9 August 2013 |access-date=10 May 2012 |work=jpnn.com}} Prabowo said he would run an investment-friendly administration if he won and that Indonesia needed more energy exploration. According to Prabowo, their enrolment is a part of Indonesia's own commitment to aid Palestine in their efforts to be a recognised sovereign country.{{Cite web |last=Koesmawardhani |first=Nograhany Widhi |title=22 Mahasiswa Palestina Dibawa ke Indonesia, Dikuliahkan Teknik-Kedokteran di Unhan |url=https://www.detik.com/edu/perguruan-tinggi/d-7027346/22-mahasiswa-palestina-dibawa-ke-indonesia-dikuliahkan-teknik-kedokteran-di-unhan |access-date=16 February 2024 |website=detikedu |language=id-ID |archive-date=14 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231114105713/https://www.detik.com/edu/perguruan-tinggi/d-7027346/22-mahasiswa-palestina-dibawa-ke-indonesia-dikuliahkan-teknik-kedokteran-di-unhan |url-status=live }} ==Presidency (2024–present)== {{Main|Post-Suharto era in Indonesia#Presidency of Prabowo (2024–present)}} {{See also|Inauguration of Prabowo Subianto}} [[File:Prabowo Subianto takes oath as president of Indonesia.jpg|thumb|President Prabowo taking his presidential oath in 2024]] The [[Prabowo Subianto 2024 presidential campaign|Prabowo–Gibran ticket]] won the [[2024 Indonesian presidential election|2024 presidential election]] with 58.59% of the vote against two of their opponents, [[Anies Baswedan 2024 presidential campaign|Anies–Muhaimin]] and [[Ganjar Pranowo 2024 presidential campaign|Ganjar–Mahfud]]. On 20 October 2024, Prabowo assumed the presidency of Indonesia. At 73 years, three days of age on inauguration day, Prabowo is the [[List of presidents of Indonesia#By age|oldest person to assume Indonesian presidency]], while his counterpart, Gibran, is the [[List of vice presidents of Indonesia#By age|youngest person to assume the Indonesian vice presidency]] at 37 years, 19 days of age.{{Cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/former-special-forces-commander-prabowo-take-up-indonesian-presidency-2024-10-19/|title=Former Special Forces commander Prabowo take up Indonesian presidency|date=19 October 2024|work=Reuters}} ===Cabinet=== {{Main|Red and White Cabinet}} On 21 October, Prabowo unveiled the [[Red and White Cabinet|largest ministerial cabinet]] in Indonesia since the [[Revised Dwikora Cabinet]] of President [[Sukarno]] in 1966, composed of 103 members including 48 ministers and 55 deputy ministers.{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c756204q2k5o |title=Indonesia leader sworn in with largest cabinet in decades |date=21 October 2024 |work=BBC}}{{Cite news|url=https://apnews.com/article/indonesia-new-cabinet-prabowo-subianto-6b1f915d584c823aa16dbc38374c739c |title=New President Subianto swears in Indonesia's largest Cabinet since 1966, with 109 members |date=21 October 2024 |work=Associated Press}} Some ministers from the previous [[Onward Indonesia Cabinet]] such as [[Airlangga Hartarto]], [[Sri Mulyani]] and [[Bahlil Lahadalia]] were retained as ministers in this cabinet. On 25 October, he held a military-style retreat for his cabinet at the [[Indonesian Military Academy]] in [[Magelang]].{{cite news|title=Indonesia's new President and ministers begin a military-style retreat which includes morning drills |url=https://apnews.com/article/indonesia-prabowo-subianto-military-retreat-af8cec0a57ba334a1f39912e89d1609a |access-date=26 October 2024 |work=Associated Press News |date=25 October 2024 |language=en}} Prabowo has conducted three cabinet reshuffles. On 19 February 2025, Minister of Higher Education, Science, and Technology [[Satryo Brodjonegoro]] resigned on 19 February 2025 and was promptly replaced by [[Brian Yuliarto]]. Satryo Brodjonegoro resigned because he believed his performance during his four months in office had not met the Prabowo administration's expectations.{{Cite web |title=Alasan Satryo Mundur dari Mendikti: Tidak Sesuai Harapan Pemerintah |url=https://www.cnnindonesia.com/nasional/20250219161921-32-1200103/alasan-satryo-mundur-dari-mendikti-tidak-sesuai-harapan-pemerintah |access-date=2026-07-05 |website=nasional |language=id-ID}}{{Cite web |last=antaranews.com |date=2025-02-19 |title=Higher education minister resigns over underperformance |url=https://en.antaranews.com/news/345513/higher-education-minister-resigns-over-underperformance |access-date=2026-07-05 |website=Antara News |language=en}} Following [[August 2025 Indonesian protests|August 2025 protests]], Prabowo replaced five ministers on 8 September, including finance minister [[Sri Mulyani Indrawati]] and security minister [[Budi Gunawan]].{{cite news |title=Indonesian leader fires ministers of finance and security after deadly protests |url=https://apnews.com/article/indonesia-protests-ministers-fired-3776bd9365804cda9f7c3f85b2104502 |work=AP News |date=8 September 2025 |language=en}} The [[Ministry of Hajj and Umrah (Indonesia)|Ministry of Hajj and Umrah]] was established as a separate ministry, assuming responsibility for the administration and management of Indonesia's Hajj pilgrimage.{{Cite web |last=detikcom |first=Tim |title=5 Fakta Reshuffle Kabinet Prabowo yang Kedua |url=https://news.detik.com/berita/d-8102511/5-fakta-reshuffle-kabinet-prabowo-yang-kedua |access-date=2026-07-05 |website=detiknews |language=id-ID}} On 17 September, the president implemented cabinet reshuffle for the Coordinating Minister for Political and Security Affairs and the Minister of Youth and Sports, replaced the Chief of Presidential Staff, the Head of Presidential Communication Office, the Deputy Heads of National Nutrition Agency, and three deputy ministers. The president also appointed the Police Commissioner General (Ret.) [[Ahmad Dofiri]] as the Special Advisor of the President for Security and Public Order and Police Reform.{{Cite web |last=Yanwardhana |first=Emir |title=Prabowo Reshuffle Kabinet, Berhentikan Erick Thohir Hingga Hasan Nasbi |url=https://www.cnbcindonesia.com/news/20250917150644-4-667813/prabowo-reshuffle-kabinet-berhentikan-erick-thohir-hingga-hasan-nasbi |access-date=2026-07-05 |website=CNBC Indonesia |language=id}}{{Cite web |last=TV |first=Metro |title=Presiden Prabowo Resmi Lantik 11 Pejabat Kabinet Merah Putih Hasil Reshuffle |url=https://www.metrotvnews.com/read/KvJCLdDg-presiden-prabowo-resmi-lantik-11-pejabat-kabinet-merah-putih-hasil-reshuffle |access-date=2026-07-05 |website=https://www.metrotvnews.com |language=id}} ===Economy=== [[File:Prabowo Subianto in Brussels - 2025 - P067555-851029.jpg|thumb|Prabowo with EU Commission President [[Ursula von der Leyen]] at the [[Berlaymont building]], 13 July 2025]] Prabowo's economic policy claim to emulate his father's, [[Sumitro Djojohadikusumo]], who had a [[Socialist economics|socialist economic]] outlook. This was further confirmed by his younger brother, [[Hashim Djojohadikusumo|Hashim]] that Prabowo's term as president will be the "right momentum" to apply his father's theories into practice and the proposed policies that will be enacted by Prabowo were the dreams hoped by their father that is soon to be realised.{{Cite web |author=MFakhriansyah |title=Prabowo Pakai 'Jurus' Ekonomi ala Sang Papi Sumitro, Begini Konsepnya |url=https://www.cnbcindonesia.com/entrepreneur/20241023100454-25-582303/prabowo-pakai-jurus-ekonomi-ala-sang-papi-sumitro-begini-konsepnya |access-date=31 January 2025 |website=CNBC Indonesia |language=id}}{{Cite news |title=Hashim: Program Prabowo Cita-cita Papi Sumitro Djojohadikusumo |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241112210319/https://www.cnnindonesia.com/ekonomi/20241024141823-532-1159169/hashim-program-prabowo-cita-cita-papi-sumitro-djojohadikusumo |archive-date=12 November 2024 |access-date=31 January 2025 |work=ekonomi |language=id-ID |url-status=live }} Among his father's economic policies, Prabowo is once seen to revive his father's ''Program Benteng'' policy, which was enacted during [[Mohammad Natsir]]'s government that empowers indigenous business owners.{{Cite web |date=7 December 2024 |title=Program Benteng Digagas Sumitro, Dihidupkan Prabowo |url=https://www.inilah.com/program-benteng-digagas-sumitro-dihidupkan-prabowo |access-date=31 January 2025 |website=Inilah.com}} His economic policies also draw inspiration from his father-in-law, [[Suharto]], with [[Coordinating Ministry for Economic Affairs|Coordinating Minister for Economic Affairs]] [[Airlangga Hartarto]] remarking that Suharto's economic policies on investments, spending and exports may be again enacted but unlike Suharto, Prabowo will be eyeing more towards digital economy, downstreaming and semiconductors.{{Cite news |title=Prabowo Akan Pakai Rumus Soeharto Capai |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241212113816/https://www.cnnindonesia.com/ekonomi/20241211191308-92-1176343/prabowo-akan-pakai-rumus-soeharto-capai-pertumbuhan-ekonomi-8-persen |archive-date=12 December 2024 |access-date=31 January 2025 |work=[[CNN Indonesia]] |language=id-ID |url-status=live }} Prabowo officially launched Indonesia's first-ever bullion bank service on 26 February 2025. For years, gold mined in Indonesia has often flowed overseas without proper domestic storage. With the launch of the bullion bank, Prabowo hopes to provide a more structured system for the storage, management, and trade of gold within the country.{{Cite web |date=26 February 2025 |title=Prabowo inaugurates Indonesia's first bullion bank service |url=https://www.idnfinancials.com/news/52742/prabowo-resmikan-layanan-bank-emas-pertama-di-indonesia |access-date=27 February 2025 |website=idnfinancials |language=en}} [[File:Prabowo-Mark Carney Sept 2025.jpg|thumb|Subianto and Canadian Prime Minister [[Mark Carney]] in [[Parliament Hill]], Ottawa, 24 September 2025]] In September 2025, Subianto and Canadian Prime Minister [[Mark Carney]] signed in Ottawa the first bilateral [[free trade]] agreement between Canada and an [[ASEAN]] member state.{{cite news |last1=Robertson |first1=Dylan |title=Canada signs ‘game-changing’ trade deal with Indonesia, new defence pact |url=https://globalnews.ca/news/11449417/canada-indonesia-trade-agreement/ |work=[[Global News]] |date=24 September 2025}} Prabowo's economic policy declares a return to a national-capitalist model grounded in the belief that the liberal free-market era has failed to deliver equitable development. At the 2025 [[St. Petersburg International Economic Forum]] he asserted that "for the past 30 years, we have seen neoliberal and free-market thinking dominate … and yet many Indonesians have not enjoyed equal opportunity."{{Cite web |date=21 June 2025 |title=President Prabowo Unveils Indonesia's People-Focused Economic Vision at SPIEF 2025 |url=https://setkab.go.id/en/president-prabowo-unveils-indonesias-people-focused-economic-vision-at-spief-2025/ |access-date=7 November 2025 |website=Sekretariat Kabinet Republik Indonesia}} Accordingly his administration pursues four strategic priorities such as food self-sufficiency, energy self-sufficiency, education quality improvement, and accelerated industrialisation, and mandates that natural-resource wealth must first benefit the people.{{Cite web |date=22 June 2025 |title=President: Economic Policy is Pro-People |url=https://investindonesia.co.id/2025/06/23/president-economic-policy-is-pro-people/ |access-date=7 November 2025 |website=Invest Indonesia |language=en-US}} In pursuit of those ends his government has launched large-scale populist spending programmes (such as the free nutritious meals scheme and rice-aid and electricity-discount policies) while simultaneously ordering a budget-efficiency sweep: a January 2025 presidential instruction cut Rp 306.6 trillion of spending to redirect funds into social programmes.{{Cite web |last=Laksono |first=Riandy |title=Why Prabowo's misguided 'austerity' is emblematic of his free-wheeling economic policy |url=https://indonesiaatmelbourne.unimelb.edu.au/why-prabowos-misguided-austerity-is-emblematic-of-his-free-wheeling-economic-policy/ |access-date=7 big budget for Indonesia achievable or overly ambitious? |url=https://www.scmp.com/week-asia/economics/article/3322349/prabowos-big-budget-indonesia-achievable-or-overly-ambitious |access-date=7 November 2025 |website=South China Morning Post |language=en}} Prabowo Subianto's decision to appoint [[Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa]] as Minister of Finance on 8 September 2025 signalled a change in economic policymaking, a departure from the fiscal-orthodoxy of his predecessor [[Sri Mulyani Indrawati]].{{Cite web |date=8 September 2025 |title=President Prabowo Appoints New Ministers, Vice Minister |url=https://setkab.go.id/en/president-prabowo-appoints-new-ministers-vice-minister/ |access-date=7 November 2025 |website=Sekretariat Kabinet Republik Indonesia}} Whereas under Sri Mulyani the |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/indonesian-finance-minister-plans-use-state-funds-boost-banking-liquidity-2025-09-10/ |access-date=8 November 2025 |work=Reuters}} In his first week, Purbaya redirected roughly Rp 200 trillion from idle government funds at the central bank into commercial banks as a measure to invigorate lending and consumption. He also stressed greater emphasis on domestic investment, real-sector productivity and boosting household purchasing power, within the broader political vision of Prabowo's "national-capitalist" economic doctrine.{{Cite news |date=9 September 2025 |title=Plain speaking economist, Purbaya, takes helm as Indonesia's finance minister |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/plain-speaking-economist-purbaya-takes-helm-indonesias-finance-minister-2025-09-09/ |access-date=8 November 2025 |work=[[Reuters]]}} He also stated that "there will be no major tax-rate increases" until Indonesia's economy grows at least 6%.{{Cite web |date=28 October 2025 |title=Purbaya: Tak ada kenaikan tarif pajak sebelum ekonomi tumbuh 6 persen |url=https://www.antaranews.com/berita/5204413/purbaya-tak-ada-kenaikan-tarif-pajak-sebelum-ekonomi-tumbuh-6-persen |access-date=7 November 2025 |website=Antara News |language=id}} ==== Bad debt ==== [[File:APEC Peru 2024 family photo.jpg|thumb|Prabowo, [[Joe Biden]], [[Anthony Albanese]], [[Justin Trudeau]] and other leaders at the [[APEC Peru 2024|APEC Summit]] in Lima, 16 November 2024]] On 5 November 2024, Prabowo signed a law that wrote off [[bad debt]] for [[small and medium enterprises]] in order to increase national economic resilience through write-offs and conditional write-offs in the fields of agriculture, plantations, animal husbandry, fisheries and maritime affairs.{{Cite web |date=10 November 2024 |title=Prabowo Hapus Piutang Macet UMKM: Maksimal Rp 500 Juta untuk Badan Usaha dan Rp 300 Juta per Individu |url=https://www.tempo.co/ekonomi/prabowo-hapus-piutang-macet-umkm-maksimal-rp-500-juta-untuk-badan-usaha-dan-rp-300-juta-per-individu-1166282 |access-date=31 January 2025 |website=Tempo |language=id}} The Write-off/Collection of Bad Debts of MSMEs is implemented as part of the 130-day work program of the Red and White Cabinet. The government stated that MSMEs are the backbone of the national economy, with a total of 66 million business units and absorbing up to 97% of the total workforce in Indonesia. However, various challenges such as the impact of the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], natural disasters, and difficult economic conditions have caused many MSME players to experience credit congestion.{{Need citation|date=November 2025}} ==== Value-added Tax Hike ==== His [[value-added tax]] policy drew controversy as the government planned to raise VAT from 11% to 12%. ==== Danantara Sovereign Wealth Fund ==== On Monday 24 February 2025, Prabowo officially launched the Daya Anagata Nusantara ([[Danantara]]) [[sovereign wealth fund]]. During the same launching speech, he also stated that the [[Red and White Cabinet|Government]] has proven its commitment with discipline and accountable financial governance.{{Cite web |date=24 February 2025 |title=President Prabowo Launches Danantara for Sustainable Investment Management|url=https://setkab.go.id/en/president-prabowo-launches-danantara-for-sustainable-investment-management/|access-date=27 February 2025 |website=Cabinet Secretariat |language=en}} Danantara works by gathering state-owned enterprise assets to seek funding. These assets will then be used as collateral for debt or even sold, which is estimated to manage up to US$900 billion in [[assets under management]]. The initial funding is targeted at US$20 billion.{{Cite web |date=24 February 2025 |title=Danantara to be Launched Today: Investment in State Assets, Targeting US$900 Billion|url=https://en.tempo.co/read/1979020/danantara-to-be-launched-today-investment-in-state-assets-targeting-us900-billion|access-date=27 February 2025 |website=Tempo|language=en}} ==== Soup Kitchens ==== Prabowo oversaw the construction of 12,000 soup kitchens. However, in 2026, the operation and construction of these kitchens were halted as a cost-cutting measure during the June and July holiday period. The public viewed the suspension as abrupt, given the substantial resources invested in the program {{cite news |last= |first= |title=Free meals operators protest BGN moratorium on new kitchens |url=https://www.thejakartapost.com/indonesia/2026/07/14/free-meals-operators-protest-bgn-moratorium-on-new-kitchens |work=The Jakarta Post |date=2026-07-14 |access-date=2026-07-17 }}. ===Defence=== policies enacted as Minister of Defence is then continued by Minister [[Sjafrie Sjamsoeddin]].{{Cite web |last=Putra |first=Nandito |date=25 November 2024 |title=Menhan Sjafrie Sjamsoeddin akan |first=Joe |date=19 April 2025 |title=Indonesia Eyes Entry in Turkey's Fifth-Gen 'KAAN' Fighter Jet Program |url=https://thedefensepost.com/2025/04/14/indonesia-turkey-kaan-fighter-jet// During the visit, President Prabowo had several important agendas, including attending the [[Board of Peace]] consultation meeting and trade negotiations with the US. Prabowo was his deputy commander at that time.{{cite book|last=Subroto|first=Hendro|year=2009|title=Sintong Panjaitan, perjalanan seorang prajurit para komando|location=Jakarta|publisher=Penerbit Buku Kompas|pages=450–453|isbn=9789797094089}} Major Luhut Pandjaitan ordered to cancel the attempt and confiscate all weapons and equipment. The threat of a coup against Suharto was later found to be false and Prabowo was given a leave due to stress.[http://m.merdeka.com/peristiwa/berpangkat-kapten-prabowo-berani-lawan-jenderal-benny-moerdani/prabowo-mau-culik-benny-moerdani.html Berpangkat Kapten, Prabowo Berani Lawan Jendral Benny Moerdani''.''] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140504191112/http://m.merdeka.com/peristiwa/berpangkat-kapten-prabowo-berani-lawan-jenderal-benny-moerdani/prabowo-mau-culik-benny-moerdani.html|date=4 May 2014}} Diakses dari situs berita Merdeka pada 3 Mei 2014 However, Prabowo denied Sintong Panjaitan's version of the story by laughing. According to him, it was unreasonable that a captain could lead his troops to fight and kidnap a general. He calmly said that every time there was a new book, there would be a new coup accusation levelled against himself, and left everyone with their own version of the story. Prabowo was once again involved in a dispute with Moerdani ahead of the [[1987 Indonesian legislative election|1988]] MPR General Assembly. According to [[Kivlan Zen]], rumours persisted that Moerdani would use his office of [[commander of the Indonesian National Armed Forces]] to gain support from the ABRI faction to run as vice president to [[Suharto]]. Prabowo reported this to Suharto and Suharto heeded Prabowo's report by replacing Moerdani with [[Try Sutrisno]] as commander of the armed forces. The position of vice president then fell to [[Sudharmono]]. Moerdani's dismissal sparked worries of a coup, however the coup never really happened. Despite this, it showed Prabowo's rising influence in the armed forces and on Suharto's decision making. ===Occupation of East Timor=== In 1983, it was claimed that Prabowo commanded the Indonesian special forces responsible for the [[Kraras massacre]]s in East Timor. The survivors of these massacres were locked up in a concentration camp guarded by Prabowo's men, where many died of starvation and ill-treatment. Prabowo claimed he was nowhere near the Viqueque district when the massacre happened, and neither the UN nor the government of Timor Leste have ever proffered charges of human rights violations against him. José Manuel Tesoro, writing for ''[[Asiaweek]]'' in 2000, contacted four separate non-governmental organisations including [[Tapol]] in London; Solidamor in Jakarta; the HAK Foundation, headquartered in [[Dili]]; and the East Timor Action Network (ETAN) in New York, but they could not provide any eyewitness reports, transcripts of intercepted communications, leaked papers, or anything that could substantiate Prabowo's involvement. ===Kidnapping of activists=== Between 1997 and 1998, Kopassus members from Team Mawar (Rose Team) were responsible for [[1997–98 activists kidnappings in Indonesia|pro-democracy activists kidnappings]] of at least 22 people mainly in Jakarta.{{cite news |last1=Nurbaiti |first1=Alya |title=Former Tim Mawar members appointed to Prabowo's office |url=https://www.thejakartapost.com/news/2020/09/25/former-tim-mawar-members-appointed-to-prabowos-office.html |access-date=19 February 2021 |work=The Jakarta Post |date=26 September 2020}} Nine activists were released and 13 remain missing.{{cite news |title=Jakarta probes missing activists |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/asia-pacific/4605931.stm |access-date=19 February 2021 |work=BBC |date=3 June 2005}} In 1999, 11 members of Tim Mawar were found guilty by a military court. However, they appealed the verdict to the Supreme Court, which was not made public and only revealed in 2007, and were never jailed and all but one remained in the military.{{cite news |last1=Harsono |first1=Andreas |title=The US Should Not Be Rehabilitating Indonesia's Abusive Special Forces |url=https://www.hrw.org/news/2018/01/26/us-should-not-be-rehabilitating-indonesias-abusive-special-forces |access-date=19 February 2021 |work=Human Rights Watch |date=26 January 2018}}{{cite news |last1=Scarpello |first1=Fabio |title=Activists outraged at promotion of disgraced Indonesian soldiers |url=https://www.scmp.com/article/594176/activists-outraged-promotion-disgraced-indonesian-soldiers |date=24 May 2007|access-date=19 February 2021 |work=South China Morning Post|url-access=subscription}} In September 2020, Defence Minister Prabowo appointed two of the Team Mawar officers, two serving [[brigadier general]]s, to senior positions in the [[Ministry of Defense (Indonesia)|Ministry of Defence]] following approval by President [[Joko Widodo]]. |website=Republika Online |language=id}} ===Allegations of authoritarianism=== As a president elected in 2024 and being [[Suharto]]'s son-in-law, Prabowo's leadership style was criticised for his authoritarian style of rule and allegedly revived the practice of ''[[Dwifungsi]]'', where active military personnel can concurrently serve in the civilian government while maintaining military command. His background as a military commander rises when ''Dwifungsi'' was at its peak of power. The [[Reformasi (Indonesia)|Reformasi]] that has sought to limit the influence of the military in civilian government has its values now threatened by moves to again empower the military, such as the revision of the Law No. 34 Year 2004.{{Citation|title=Is Indonesia marching back towards military rule?|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=C8Rpnf-usr4|date=3 April 2025|accessdate=4 April 2025|work=South China Morning Post}} During his time as defence minister under [[Joko Widodo]], Prabowo is considered to have restored the role of the military in many aspects of civilian life. He was known to involve the military in government programs such as the free meal program, food estate, and many other roles that is supposed to be done by the civilian sector. Few of his cabinet ministers also have military roles, which further strengthens the perception that the direction of government tends to revive [[New Order (Indonesia)|New Order]]-style practices. His most controversial appointment in his cabinet however is when he appointed [[Teddy Indra Wijaya]] who was still active in the military to be his [[Cabinet Secretariat (Indonesia)|cabinet secretary]], which generate criticism from academicians and legal experts saying Prabowo has violated the Law No. 34 Year 2004 Article 47 which states that active service members of the [[Indonesian National Armed Forces]] must resign or retire from military life if appointed or given a civilian role.JPNN. Prabowo Subianto Djojohadikusumo (born 17 October 1951) is an Indonesian politician, businessman, and retired military officer who has served as the eighth president of Indonesia since 2024. He previously served as the 26th minister of defence under President Joko Widodo from 2019 to 2024. Prabowo is Indonesia's third president to have a military background after Suharto and Susilo Bambang Yudhoyono and is the oldest first-term president in Indonesian history.
Prabowo graduated from the Indonesian Military Academy in 1970 and primarily served in the Special Forces (Kopassus) until he was appointed to lead the Strategic Reserves Command (Kostrad) in 1998. Later that same year, he was discharged from the military and subsequently banned from entering the United States for allegedly committing human rights abuses.
In early 2008, Prabowo's inner circle established the Gerindra Party. In the 2009 presidential election, he ran unsuccessfully for the vice presidency as Megawati Sukarnoputri's running mate. He contested the 2014 presidential election and was defeated by Jakarta governor Joko Widodo, which he initially disputed. He made another unsuccessful run for the presidency in 2019 against Joko Widodo, with Sandiaga Uno as his running mate and with the support of Gerindra, the Prosperous Justice Party (PKS), the National Mandate Party (PAN), the Democratic Party (Demokrat), and Berkarya Party. His refusal to accept the result saw his followers stage protests that sparked riots in Jakarta. However, after a heated contest, Prabowo joined Joko Widodo's cabinet as his minister of defence for the 2019 to 2024 period.
On 10 October 2021, Gerindra announced Prabowo as their candidate in the 2024 presidential election. On 12 August 2022, Prabowo announced that he accepted Gerindra's nomination. Prabowo declared victory in the election on 14 February 2024, as early unofficial polling showed him with a lead in the first round of voting. On 20 March, the General Election Commission (KPU) certified the results and declared him as the president-elect of Indonesia. The Constitutional Court (MK) confirmed his status on 22 April 2024. Prabowo was sworn in as the 8th president of Indonesia on 20 October 2024.
